steps.tx: A **Bankart lesion** constitutes the primary anatomical defect predisposing to recurrent anterior shoulder dislocation. Traumatic initial detachment of the anteroinferior labrum and inferior glenohumeral ligament complex compromises the static bumper that stabilizes the shallow glenoid cavity. In adolescents suffering a traumatic anterior dislocation, recurrence rates exceed seventy percent because this fibrous labral seal fails to reconstitute without anatomical healing.
steps.say: The essential pathology in recurrent anterior instability is a Bankart lesion. The anteroinferior labrum and inferior glenohumeral ligament avulse from the glenoid rim. Without this fibrocartilaginous bumper, the humeral head repeatedly slides over the anterior glenoid edge, especially in active teenagers.

steps.tx: A **Hill-Sachs lesion** develops concurrently as an impaction compression fracture on the posterolateral aspect of the humeral head. During anterior displacement, the softer cancellous bone of the humeral head impacts forcefully against the dense cortical anteroinferior glenoid rim. If large, the defect engages the glenoid edge during functional abduction and external rotation, mechanically levering the head out of joint.
steps.say: When the shoulder dislocates forward, the hard anterior glenoid rim dents the softer posterolateral humeral head, creating a Hill-Sachs lesion. When the arm is later abducted and externally rotated, this bony groove catches on the glenoid rim and levers the joint out.

left.title: Non-Engaging Lesion
points: Defect stays clear of glenoid edge
Managed with soft tissue Bankart repair

right.title: Engaging Lesion
points: Levers humeral head out in abduction

steps.tx: The **apprehension test** evaluates anterior instability by passively positioning the shoulder in ninety degrees of abduction and ninety degrees of maximum external rotation. The patient displays sudden muscular guarding and anxiety as the humeral head subluxates anteriorly. Squeezing the anterior humeral head posteriorly in the Jobe relocation test abolishes this distress, confirming capsulolabral incompetence rather than impingement.
steps.say: Test for anterior instability by abducting the shoulder ninety degrees and externally rotating it. The patient immediately tenses with frank apprehension. Next, press the humeral head backward in the Jobe relocation maneuver. If their pain and dread disappear, the test is unequivocally positive.

steps.tx: Arthroscopic **Bankart repair** reattaches the avulsed labrum and tightens the attenuated inferior glenohumeral ligament using suture anchors placed along the articular glenoid margin. This anatomical restoration achieves success rates above eighty-five percent in individuals without substantial bone deficiency. Patients wear an immobilizing sling for three weeks before starting progressive range of motion and rotator cuff strengthening exercises.
steps.say: Arthroscopic Bankart repair anchors the detached labrum back onto the glenoid bone rim and tightens the stretched joint capsule. It works brilliantly for soft tissue tears when glenoid bone loss remains minor. The arm is protected in a sling for three weeks before rehabilitation begins.

left.title: Indications for Bankart Repair
points: Intact glenoid bone rim without loss

steps.tx: The **Latarjet procedure** provides the definitive surgical solution when anterior glenoid bone loss exceeds twenty to twenty-five percent. In this non-anatomical reconstruction, the coracoid process with its attached conjoined tendon is transferred through the subscapularis muscle and screwed onto the deficient anterior glenoid neck. This triple-blocking effect creates a bony platform, tendon sling, and capsular barrier.
steps.say: When anterior glenoid bone loss exceeds twenty percent, soft tissue anchors fail. You must perform a Latarjet procedure. The coracoid process is osteotomized and screwed onto the anterior glenoid rim. Its attached conjoined tendon provides a dynamic muscular sling that prevents future anterior translation.

vis.title: Procedure Comparison
rows: Pure soft tissue tear, minimal bone loss
Bony augment plus conjoined tendon sling

quiz.q: What constitutes the definitive pathological lesion in a classic Bankart defect?
options: Detachment of the anteroinferior glenoid labrum
Impaction fracture of the anteromedial humeral head
Rupture of the long head of the biceps tendon
Tear of the supraspinatus tendon insertion
quiz.explain: A Bankart lesion is the traumatic avulsion of the anteroinferior glenoid labrum and attached inferior glenohumeral ligament complex from the glenoid margin.

quiz.q: Which surgical procedure is preferred when anterior glenoid bone loss exceeds 25 percent?
quiz.explain: When glenoid bone loss exceeds 20 to 25 percent (the critical bone loss threshold), soft tissue repairs fail. The Latarjet procedure transfers the coracoid with conjoined tendon to reconstruct the glenoid arc.
